title: enhanced-canary-ab-shadow-autorollback-workflow
author: Priya Patel
description:
Motivation: Production rollouts have multiple failure modes when combining canary, A/B, and shadow traffic. Teams running progressive rollouts need deterministic autorollback behavior driven by composite metrics and safety guards. This PR implements an enhanced workflow that unifies canary + A/B + shadow traffic policies, exposes observable decision points, and adds stability guards to reduce noisy rollbacks.

What this PR does: consolidated rollout controller changes to support multi-stage rollouts (canary -> A/B -> full), shadow probing windows for metric collection without impacting routing, composite metric definitions (latency P95, error-rate, regression score), and an autorollback engine that evaluates quorums and safety gates before reverting. Adds CLI and API flags for configuring staged shadow probing windows and a new rollout.status endpoint for auditability.

Design notes: - Autorollback is evaluated against a priority-ordered metric list and requires a quorum of unhealthy signals across independent cohorts. - Shadow probing windows allow the system to collect metrics from shadowed traffic for a configurable duration before enabling live routing decisions. - Safety guards include minimum sample sizes, cooldown periods, and a staged rollback path (scale-down traffic -> pause -> rollback) to avoid flapping. - Observability: emits rollout_decision events, metric_delta traces, and a per-rollout timeline accessible from the Console.

Compatibility: Works with existing model variants and fallback policies. Backwards-compatible defaults preserve current behavior when new flags are not set.

Checklist: - [x] Controller implementation and unit tests - [x] End-to-end tests for canary -> A/B -> full path - [x] Shadow probing e2e with synthetic traffic generator - [x] Console dashboard updates and rollout.status API - [x] Documentation and migration notes

Related: ENG-1284 (rollout safety), ENG-1350 (observability events), reference PRs pr-121045 and pr-131210 for earlier autorollback primitives.

review_comments: Maya Chen: High level - this looks solid. Two asks: 1) ensure we don't regress CPU/KV cache pressure during shadow probing, 2) add an opt-out flag for teams that only want classic canaries.
Priya Patel (author): Added cpu budget check and opt-out flag (feature gates.rollouts.unified = false). Updated tests to verify opt-out behavior.
Liam O'Connor: Noted a concurrency race in controller.go where status updates could be lost on quick successive events. Please add a compare-and-swap loop or retry.
Priya Patel (author): Addressed with an optimistic update loop and test covering concurrent updates. Also added a metric rollout_status_conflict_retries.
Diego Rivera: Observability events look good. Can we add an example Grafana dashboard with the composite metric panels?
Priya Patel (author): Included dashboard JSON and Console wiring in this PR; dashboards live under web/console/src/dashboards/rollout.json.
Maya Chen: CI flake on e2e/probing_shadow_test — rerunning. If it flakes again we should mock timeouts (see last commit).
CI rerun resolved the e2e flake after deterministic time mocks were added.
ci_checks: e2e-rollout: runs synthetic traffic suite — pass (flaky fixed on rerun)
merge_outcome: merged (squash) by Maya Chen after approvals and CI green
release_notes: Added unified rollout workflow: multi-stage canary/A-B/full, shadow probing windows, composite metric autorollback with safety guards, extended observability (rollout_decision events and rollout.status endpoint).
